A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UMAP force-analysis research. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original embedding experiments, including 100-run initialization comparisons, learning-rate sweeps and a PubMed embedding evaluation.

after.justification: v4 retains original embedding experiments and adds quantitative diagnostics, additional datasets, controlled flip experiments and synthetic stress-test results.

M1.justification: The main modified-attraction, composite-schedule and modified-repulsion procedures in Eqs. (13)–(15) remain unchanged. v4 removes the optional cross-method hybrid force procedures in v3 Appendix J and introduces an experimental probabilistic flip-update variant in Appendix M.

E1.justification: v4 adds Shekhar retinal-cell data, 20 Newsgroups and the synthetic Separated-Neighbor scenario, which places an isolated neighboring pair across repelling points. It removes v3 Appendix C’s 300,000-sample PubMed/PubMedBERT study. MNIST, FMNIST and Macosko transcriptomes remain.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain default UMAP, UMAP with a=b=1, NEG-t-SNE and PaCMAP; the PaCMAP and LocalMAP appendix analyses also remain. The PCA-initialized reference already appears in v3, although v4 expands its quantitative reporting.

E3.justification: v4 introduces Spearman correlation, epoch-level flip/expansion measurements and normalized neighbor-distance measurements. New protocols include flip-probability interventions and 400-epoch synthetic tests with N=500, 1000 and 5000. The retained learning-rate sweeps preserve their reported settings.

E4.justification: New analyses examine a and b>1 sensitivity, MNIST handwriting substructure, alternative flip estimators, pair trajectories, controlled flip injection and the Separated-Neighbor stress test (Appendices F–H and L–N). v3’s separate mix-and-match force analysis is removed.

E5.justification: v3 already reports 100 random initializations and Procrustes means and standard deviations. v4 Table 2 additionally reports uncertainty for embedding-quality metrics and explicitly includes 100-run PCA-initialized controls. It does not establish an increase beyond 100 random starts.

E6.justification: v4 adds Tables 1–3 and new dynamics, sensitivity and stress-test results. For example, Table 3 reports trustworthiness falling from 0.9588 to 0.9306 as injected flip probability increases. v3’s PubMed k-NN result of 49.2% versus 55.48% and hybrid-force results are removed. Retained learning-rate plots are unchanged. New Shekhar and 20NG Procrustes summaries disagree between Table 2 and Figures 12–13.

T1.justification: The original contraction/expansion propositions and method-comparison proofs are retained. v4 adds formal flip definitions and translation-invariance reasoning in Appendix L, a distance-rescaling derivation for a in Appendix G, and a two-threshold analysis for b>1 in Appendix F.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces v3’s broad claim of making embedding methods more interpretable, robust and accurate with the narrower claim of providing mechanistic understanding. The principal contributions concerning force shapes, annealing, initialization consistency and cluster formation remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations connecting injected flips to quality degradation, parameter scaling to finite optimization, and cluster substructure to handwriting styles. It also explains flip-detector limitations, discusses two dominant 20NG modes, and warns that additional clusters may represent over-fragmentation rather than meaningful structure.

D1.justification: v4 adds dataset sizes, class counts and PCA preprocessing documentation, Shekhar/20NG access information, flip-estimator and intervention procedures, and detailed synthetic graph and initialization construction. The core exact k=15 graph, Numba and Procrustes implementation disclosures remain. PubMed visualization-code instructions are removed.

R1.justification: v4 adds references including Yang et al. (2009), Lu and Calder (2025), Oppenheim and Lim (1981), and dataset citations, while removing Gu et al. (2021). The NEG-t-SNE equivalence proposition now explicitly credits Damrich et al. (2023). The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v4 reorganizes the main analysis, moving the NEG-t-SNE comparison from Section 6 to Section 5.1. It rewrites the conclusion and roadmaps, expands explanatory passages about force dynamics and optimization, and substantially restructures the appendix narrative.

P2.justification: v3 Figure 1 is reorganized into v4 Figures 1 and 3. v4 adds three tables, diagnostic plots and handwriting-detail panels, removes PubMed and hybrid-force figures, and adopts TMLR typography and layout. Many retained appendix plots are renumbered and repositioned without changing their contents.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens the mechanistic account through optimization diagnostics, sensitivity/stress tests and explicit quality-versus-consistency measurements, while narrowing the abstract’s accuracy claim. Some application and design evidence is lost with the PubMed and hybrid examples. Conflicting Procrustes summaries in Table 2 versus Figures 12–13, and Appendix M’s positive-fa intervention rule despite fa being defined as nonpositive, limit confidence in the added evidence and keep the net improvement modest.
